questions.q: Besides the ICT cascade, which causes of secondary brain damage are printed?
questions.exp: Causes : Haemorrhagic transformation; SIADH → hyponatremia (Book p700)

questions.q: Suspected TIA is investigated with:

questions.q: Step 4 of the imaging work-up is:

questions.q: The infarct core is delineated on:

units.title: 1. Goals of Stroke Management
units.guide:
The goals of treatment are recanalisation/reperfusion, preventing secondary brain damage and optimising collateral blood flow.
The printed causes of secondary brain damage are the raised intracranial pressure cascade — ↑ICT from cerebral oedema leading to herniation/coning — plus haemorrhagic transformation and SIADH with hyponatraemia.
Each goal maps to a threat: reperfusion to the infarct core, secondary-damage prevention to oedema and metabolic injury, and collateral flow to the penumbra.

units.title: 2. Immediate Management and the CT Protocol
units.guide:
Immediate management is used when the onset of stroke is known: the CT protocol table maps scenarios to investigations — presentation within 6 hours needs no additional imaging, suspected TIA needs diffusion-weighted MRI to rule out stroke, and presentation within 4.5 hours of symptom onset with CT excluding bleed proceeds to thrombolysis with alteplase 0.9 mg/kg (10% bolus, 90% infusion over 1 hour) or tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg IV bolus, which can be given without CT angiogram if thrombolysis is indicated.
The steps are supportive care with oxygen and vitals, checking random blood sugar, ECG plus troponin I, and BP correction — labetalol 20 mg IV up to two times when BP is ≥220/110 mmHg, or above 185/110 mmHg when thrombolysis or thrombectomy is planned.
Step 5 is CT: plain CT to rule out bleed, then CT angiography.

units.title: 3. Thrombolysis Contraindications
units.guide:
The printed contraindications to thrombolysis are age under 18 years, BP above 185/110 despite treatment, CT hypodensity over one third, intra-axial neoplasm, aortic dissection or infective endocarditis, recent heparin within 48 hours or LMWH within 24 hours, platelet count under 1,00,000 cells/μl, bleeding within the last 3 weeks (especially GI bleed) and surgery, trauma or stroke within the last 3 months.
Each item is an absolute block to the 4.5-hour alteplase/tenecteplase pathway.

units.title: 4. CT and the MRI Protocol for Wake-up Stroke
units.guide:
The printed order continues on p701 with step 5 — CT: plain CT to rule out bleed, then CT angiography.
The MRI protocol is used for wake-up stroke, when the time of onset is unknown: diffusion-weighted MRI first establishes the diagnosis (hyperintense white lesions = stroke); the T2 FLAIR sequence then times the event, the lesion appearing white or black depending on how long ago the patient presented; a DWI-white versus FLAIR-black mismatch is indicative of very new onset, and such a patient can be considered for thrombolysis — ADC (apparent diffusion coefficient) is then performed to confirm restricted diffusion.

units.title: 5. Perfusion Imaging and the Penumbra
units.guide:
Step 4 is perfusion imaging, which compares DWI and PWI: the infarct core shows on DWI, part of the penumbra appears on PWI, and the complete penumbra is the region identified on MR perfusion imaging — the PWI-DWI mismatch (PDM).
The printed CBF thresholds are below 10 ml/100 g/min for infarcted tissue, above 20 ml/100 g/min for normal perfusion, and 10-20 ml/100 g/min for the penumbra region.

units.title: 6. Management After 24 Hours
units.guide:
After 24 hours the printed sequence is: repeat imaging; anticoagulation for cardioembolic stroke — for valvular AF only warfarin is used, the causes printed being mitral stenosis and prosthetic valve; antiplatelet therapy — single (aspirin in most cases) or dual temporarily as aspirin plus ticagrelor for corresponding cardiac disease, minor stroke/TIA and ICAD over 50%; carotid endarterectomy over carotid stenting — endarterectomy for all cases except high-risk cardiac cases, stenting used in high-risk cardiac cases; and cholesterol management with target LDL below 100 on atorvastatin/rosuvastatin.
Indications for both revascularisation procedures are over 50% block in a symptomatic patient and over 70% block in an asymptomatic patient.
